- <LinkCard title="Crates" href="/reference/crates/" description="What each workspace crate contains." />


---

---
title: Macros
description: API reference for component!, quoin_render!, quoin_element!, effect!, and run_app!.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

All parsing and code generation lives in `quoin-macros-core`; the `quoin-macros` crate is the `proc_macro` boundary. The backend dispatch selects exactly one framework — enabling two framework features is a compile error, by design.

Import: `use quoin_macros::{component, effect, quoin_element, quoin_render, run_app};` (re-exported through the `quoin` facade when a framework feature is enabled).

## component!

Defines a framework-agnostic reactive component. Recognized blocks:

| Block | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `props` | Typed input fields with defaults, e.g. `initial_count: u32 = 0`. |
| `state` | Reactive fields with initial values; each becomes a signal. |
| `globals` | Global values retrieved from context; suffix `observe` to track changes. |
| `on_mount` / `on_unmount` | Lifecycle hooks run at mount / unmount. |
| `fn …` | Actions — plain functions over the state signals. |
| `render` | The view tree; runs each render pass. |

Framework output: a `struct` with a `Render` impl (GPUI), `#[component] fn … -> impl IntoView` (Leptos), `#[component] fn … -> Element` (Dioxus).

## quoin_render!

JSX-like declarative UI with Tailwind class transpilation.

| Syntax | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `div(class: "…") { … }` | Element with classes and children. |
| `if[cond] { … }` | Conditional subtree. |
| `for[item in items] { … }` | Repetition over an iterable. |
| `attr: value` | Named attribute (classes, handlers, configuration). |
| `on_click: \|ev\| …` | Handler receiving a [typed event](/reference/events/). |

Element vocabulary includes `div`, `button`, `tabs`/`tab`, `data_table`/`column`, `virtual_list`, `dropdown_menu`, `input`, `checkbox`, `radio`, `switch`, `slider`, `icon`, `badge`, `tooltip`, `progress`, `skeleton`, `scroll_area`, `separator`, `styled_text`, and `clipboard_button`.

## quoin_element!

Declares a named custom element with typed props and a render closure:

<Code lang="rust" code={`quoin_element!("my-widget", { width: u32 }, |props| quoin_render! { div { "w" } });`} />

## effect!

Runs side effects reactively. Two syntaxes:

| Form | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| Legacy | `effect! { watch: [signal], \|\| … }` |
| Structured | `effect! { deps: […], run: \|\| …, cleanup: \|\| … }` — `cleanup` optional |

Expansion per framework: `create_effect` + `on_cleanup` (Leptos), `use_effect` + `use_drop` (Dioxus), run-on-execute + cleanup-on-drop (GPUI).

## run_app!

Bootstraps the application with a single line.

| Form | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `run_app!(MyComponent)` | GPUI with default window options; Leptos/Dioxus mount to body. |
| `run_app!(MyComponent, window_opts: custom_opts)` | GPUI with custom window options. |

<Aside type="note">
  To inspect the generated code for a component, run `just expand component="ucp-lib" feature="gpui"` from the repository root.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Declarative UI Macros" href="/guides/ui-macros/" description="Worked examples for every macro." />
- <LinkCard title="Styling with Tailwind Classes" href="/guides/styling/" description="How class strings compile to native styling." />


---

---
title: Reactive Context
description: API reference for the ReactiveContext trait and the ReactiveContextExt extension methods.
type: reference
---

import { Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`ReactiveContext` is the entry point for creating signals and accessing framework services. Adapter crates provide the concrete implementations (`GpuiContext`, `LeptosContext`, …); your code depends only on the trait.

Import: `use quoin_core::prelude::*;`

## ReactiveContext methods

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Signal` (assoc.) | `type Signal<T: Clone + Send + 'static>: Signal<T>` | The adapter's signal type. |
| `Executor` (assoc.) | `type Executor: Executor` | The adapter's executor type. |
| `create_signal` | `fn create_signal<T: Clone + Send + 'static>(&self, initial: T) -> Self::Signal<T>` | Creates reactive state. |
| `executor` | `fn executor(&self) -> Self::Executor` | Returns the async task spawner. |
| `request_update` | `fn request_update(&self)` | Marks the UI as dirty. |
| `provide_global` | `fn provide_global<T: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static>(&self, value: T)` | Stores an app-wide value keyed by type. |
| `use_global` | `fn use_global<T: Clone + 'static + Send + Sync>(&self) -> Option<Self::Signal<T>>` | Returns a handle to the stored global, if present. Every adapter returns a handle to the same shared cell. |

## ReactiveContextExt methods

Blanket-implemented over every `ReactiveContext`; included in the prelude.

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_resource` | `fn create_resource<T, E, F, Fut>(&self, fetch: F) -> Resource<…>` | Creates an async data resource with race-free reloads and cooperative cancellation. |
| `batch` | `fn batch<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce() -> R) -> R` | Runs `f` inside a batch scope and issues a single update request afterwards. |
| `update_global` | `fn update_global<T, R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut T) -> R) -> R` | Mutates a stored global; type-keyed access. |
| `use_global_or_init` | `fn use_global_or_init<T>(&self, init: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Self::Signal<T>` | Returns the global handle, initializing it on first use. |

## Example

<Code lang="rust" code={`let signal = cx.create_signal(0);            // create reactive state
let executor = cx.executor();                // async task spawner
cx.request_update();                         // mark UI as dirty

cx.provide_global(Theme::Dark);
if let Some(theme) = cx.use_global::<Theme>() {
    let current = theme.get();
}

let res = cx.create_resource(|token| async move { /* fetch */ });
cx.batch(|| { a.set(1); b.set(2); });        // one update request
let settings = cx.use_global_or_init(Settings::default);`} />

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Sharing Global State" href="/guides/global-state/" description="Task-focused guide to provide_global, update_global, and use_global_or_init." />
- <LinkCard title="Executors & Tasks" href="/reference/executors/" description="What the executor returned by cx.executor() can do." />


---

---
title: Resources
description: API reference for Resource and ResourceState — the async data loading primitive shared by all adapters.
type: reference
---

import { Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Resource` models the full lifecycle of an async computation whose result feeds the UI. It is the framework-agnostic equivalent of Leptos' `Resource` and Dioxus' `use_resource`, and works on every adapter because it is built from two primitives every adapter provides: a `Signal` and an `Executor`.

Import: `use quoin_core::prelude::*;`

## Lifecycle

<Code lang="text" code={`Idle → Loading → Ready(T) | Failed(E)`} />

Every reload cancels the in-flight request and returns the resource to `Loading`. A generation counter makes reloads race-free: a stale request can never overwrite a newer one's result.

## ResourceState

| Variant | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Idle` | Created but not started, or cancelled after starting. |
| `Loading` | A request is in flight. |
| `Ready(T)` | The latest request completed successfully. |
| `Failed(Arc<E>)` | The latest request failed. |

## Resource methods

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `fn state(&self) -> &S` | Returns the signal holding the current `ResourceState` — read it reactively from the UI. |
| `read` | `fn read(&self) -> Option<T>` | Convenience read of the current `Ready` value, if any. |
| `reload_with` | `fn reload_with<C, F, Fut>(&self, cx: &C, fetch: F)` | Re-runs the fetch closure on the given context, cancelling any in-flight request. |

## Creating a resource

Created via `ReactiveContextExt::create_resource`; cloning a `Resource` shares the same underlying state.

<Code lang="rust" code={`let user = cx.create_resource(|token| async move {
    // Real fetch here; check \`token.is_cancelled()\` between awaits.
    Ok::<User, FetchError>(fetch_user(&token).await?)
});

// UI reads:
match user.state().get() {
    ResourceState::Loading => spinner(),
    ResourceState::Ready(user) => profile(&user),
    ResourceState::Failed(err) => error(&err),
    ResourceState::Idle => placeholder(),
}

// Reload — cancels the in-flight request first:
user.reload_with(&cx, fetch_user_closure);`} />

## Design guarantees

- **Race-free** — generation counting; stale responses are discarded.
- **Cooperative cancellation** — reloads cancel the in-flight request via its `CancellationToken` and abort the task through the executor's join handle.
- **Reactive** — the state lives in a framework signal, so UI reads re-render automatically on transitions.

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Loading Async Data" href="/guides/async-data/" description="Task-focused guide with fetch, reload, and cancellation patterns." />
- <LinkCard title="Cancellation Tokens" href="/reference/cancellation/" description="The token handed to the fetch closure." />


---

---
title: Signals
description: API reference for the Signal trait and the SignalExt extension methods available on every adapter.
type: reference
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`Signal<T>` is a readable and writable reactive value. Signals are `Clone`, which makes them convenient to pass into closures and store in structs. Every adapter implements the same trait, and the blanket `SignalExt` extension adds convenience methods with zero per-adapter overhead.

Import: `use quoin_core::prelude::*;`

## Signal methods

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get` | `fn get(&self) -> T` | Returns a clone of the current value. |
| `with` | `fn with<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&T) -> R) -> R` | Borrows the value without cloning. |
| `set` | `fn set(&self, value: T)` | Writes the value and requests an update. |
| `set_if_eq` | `fn set_if_eq(&self, value: T) -> bool` where `T: PartialEq` | Writes only when the value differs; returns `true` when written. Single-lock implementations override this for a cheaper compare-and-write. |
| `update` | `fn update(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut T))` | Mutates the value in place. |

## SignalExt methods

| Method | Signature | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_eq` | `fn set_eq(&self, value: T) -> bool` where `T: PartialEq` | Delegates to `set_if_eq`; skipping equal writes removes wasted re-render requests on pull-based adapters. |
| `replace` | `fn replace(&self, value: T) -> T` | Sets the value and returns the previous one. |
| `take` | `fn take(&self) -> T` where `T: Default` | Replaces the value with `T::default()` and returns the old value. |
| `map` | `fn map<U, F>(&self, f: F) -> Derived<Self, T, U, F>` | Sugar for `derived(self, f)` — a read-only computed view. |

## Example

<Code lang="rust" code={`let signal = cx.create_signal(42u32);
assert_eq!(signal.get(), 42);
signal.with(|v| println!("{v}"));   // borrow without cloning
signal.set(100);
signal.update(|v| *v += 1);
assert_eq!(signal.get(), 101);

signal.set_eq(101);                 // false — unchanged, no update requested
let old = signal.replace(7);        // old == 101
let taken = signal.take();          // taken == 7, signal now 0`} />

<Aside type="note">
  On pull-based adapters (GPUI, Xilem) every mutation calls `request_update()`. Prefer `set_eq` for values that frequently receive equal writes.
</Aside>

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Derived Signals & Memos" href="/reference/derived/" description="Computed views, memoization, and zipped signals." />
- <LinkCard title="Reactive Context" href="/reference/reactive-context/" description="Where signals are created and how update requests flow." />

---
title: quoin-testkit
description: API reference for TestContext, the deterministic executors, and UpdateRecorder in quoin-testkit.
type: reference
---

import { Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`quoin-testkit` provides concrete, dependency-light implementations of the core traits designed for tests. Reactive business logic written against `ReactiveContext` runs headlessly — no window manager, no browser, fully deterministic.

Import: `use quoin_testkit::{TestContext, ImmediateExecutor, …};` or through the facade with the `testkit` feature.

## Components

| Component | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `TestContext` | Full `ReactiveContext` with update counting and a shared global store. Construct with `TestContext::with_executor(executor)`. |
| `ImmediateExecutor` | Runs futures inline to completion — fully deterministic, but blocking. |
| `ThreadedExecutor` | Runs each future on a dedicated thread — real concurrency, real abort semantics. |
| `TokioExecutor` *(feature `tokio`)* | Runs futures on a real tokio runtime; `sleep` delegates to `tokio::time::sleep`, so paused-time tests (`start_paused` + `advance`) drive executor timers deterministically. |
| `UpdateRecorder` | Assert how many times the UI was asked to re-render. |
| `TestSignal<T>` | Standalone thread-safe signal backed by `Arc<RwLock<T>>`; mutations bump the owning context's update counter, mirroring pull-based adapters. |

## TestContext API

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `with_executor(e)` | Builds a context around the chosen executor. |
| `updates()` | Returns the update recorder; `.count()` gives the number of re-render requests so far. |

## Executor selection

| You are testing | Choose |
| --- | --- |
| Pure state machines, reducers, derived pipelines | `ImmediateExecutor` — synchronous and deterministic |
| Logic that awaits timers/channels; abort/detach semantics | `ThreadedExecutor` or `TokioExecutor` |

`ImmediateExecutor` cannot model mid-flight cancellation because futures finish before the handle exists.

## Example

<Code lang="rust" code={`use quoin_core::prelude::*;
use quoin_testkit::{ImmediateExecutor, TestContext};

let mut cx = TestContext::with_executor(ImmediateExecutor);
let count = cx.create_signal(0u32);
count.set(41);
count.update(|v| *v += 1);
assert_eq!(count.get(), 42);
assert_eq!(cx.updates().count(), 2, "set + update each requested a re-render");`} />

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Testing with quoin-testkit" href="/guides/testing/" description="Task-focused guide with batching and store test patterns." />
- <LinkCard title="Executors & Tasks" href="/reference/executors/" description="The production-side executor contract the testkit mirrors." />

---
title: Universal Component Protocol
description: API reference for the quoin-ui traits, node types, and variant enums that abstract rich widgets across frameworks.
type: reference
---

import { Code, LinkCard } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The `quoin-ui` crate defines framework-agnostic adapter traits for complex UI components. Adapter crates such as `quoin-ui-gpui` provide concrete implementations. Your code depends on the traits; the framework feature pulls in the implementation.

Import: `use quoin_ui::{ButtonAdapter, ButtonVariant, ComponentSize, …};`

## Adapter traits

| Trait | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `VirtualListAdapter` | Efficiently render large, scrollable lists (marker trait, `Default + Clone + Send + Sync`). |
| `TableAdapter` | Sortable, striped data tables. |
| `TextInputAdapter` | Two-way bound text inputs. |
| `ButtonAdapter` | Styled buttons (primary, ghost, destructive). |
| `DropdownMenuAdapter` | Dropdown menus with items. |
| `TabBarAdapter` | Tab navigation. |
| `Clipboard` | Read/write the system clipboard. |
| `QuoinTheme` | Theme token resolution. |

## Node vocabulary

The `node` module models widget trees as typed nodes, produced by factory functions:

| Factory / node | Models |
| --- | --- |
| `div` → `DivNode`, `DivBuilder` | Containers with styling. |
| `text` → `TextNode`, `StyledTextNode` | Text runs with `NodeFontWeight`. |
| `button` → `ButtonNode` | Buttons with `NodeButtonVariant` and `NodeKeySpec`. |
| `input` → `InputNode` | Text inputs with `InputValues`. |
| `data_table` → `TableNode`, `ColumnSpec` | Tables with per-column specs and `ScrollRestorationNode` support. |
| `virtual_list` → `VirtualListNode` | Windowed lists. |
| `tab_bar` → `TabBarNode`, `TabSpec` | Tab bars. |
| `dropdown_menu` → `MenuItem`, `MenuProvider` | Menus. |
| `icon` → `IconNode` | Icons. |
| `clipboard` → `ClipboardNode` | Copy-to-clipboard affordances. |
| `custom` → `CustomNode` | Escape hatch for arbitrary widgets, with `NodeEventCtx` and `NodeHandler`. |

Supporting types: `Node`, `NodeChild`, `NodeEnv`, `NodeFactory`, `NodeStyle`, `StyleCmd`.

## Variant enums

| Enum | Variants | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ComponentSize` | `Small`, `Medium`, `Large` | `Medium` |
| `SortDirection` | `None`, `Asc`, `Desc` | `None` |
| `ButtonVariant` | Struct with `primary: bool`, `ghost: bool`, `destructive: bool`, `size: ComponentSize` | — |
| `NodeKeySpec` | Key handling specs for focusable nodes | — |

## Example

<Code lang="rust" code={`use quoin_ui::{ButtonAdapter, ButtonVariant, ComponentSize};

let adapter = GpuiButtonAdapter::default();
let button = adapter.render(Some("Click Me".into()), ButtonVariant {
    primary: true,
    size: ComponentSize::Medium,
    ..Default::default()
});`} />

## Next steps

- <LinkCard title="Composing UCP Components" href="/guides/ucp-components/" description="Task-focused guide to tables, lists, and buttons." />
- <LinkCard title="Feature Flags" href="/reference/feature-flags/" description="The ui feature and its per-adapter availability." />

---
title: Build a Cross-Framework Counter
description: The golden-path tutorial — install Quoin, write a portable counter hook, render it in GPUI, then re-target the same hook to another framework.
type: tutorial
---

import { Aside, Code, LinkCard, Steps, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

You will build a counter application whose reactive logic lives in a framework-agnostic library crate and whose view layer runs on GPUI. At the end you re-target the same hook to Leptos by changing a single feature flag. The counter is the smallest program that exercises every layer of Quoin: a [signal](/reference/signals/) for state, a portable hook written against [`ReactiveContext`](/reference/reactive-context/), and a framework view that reads the signal.

**Prerequisites:** Rust stable 1.88 or newer (`rustup update stable`), and a terminal. No GPUI system libraries are needed for the logic crate; GPUI itself needs the usual Linux windowing headers listed in the [installation guide](/guides/installation/#prerequisites).

## Create the project

<Steps>
1. Create a Cargo workspace with two crates: a library for the portable logic and a binary for the GPUI view.

    <Code lang="sh" code={`cargo new counter --lib
cargo new counter-gpui --bin`} />

2. Add Quoin to both manifests. The library depends on `quoin-core` (traits only, no framework). The binary depends on `quoin` with the `gpui` feature.

    <Code lang="toml" code={`# counter/Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
quoin-core = "0.1"`} />

    <Code lang="toml" code={`# counter-gpui/Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
counter = { path = "../counter" }
quoin = { version = "0.1", features = ["gpui"] }`} />

    <Aside type="caution">
      The version on crates.io may lag the repository. If you are building against a checkout of the [Quoin repository](https://github.com/elcoosp/quoin), use path dependencies instead, as the examples in the repository do:

      <Code lang="toml" code={`quoin = { path = "../quoin", features = ["gpui"] }`} />
    </Aside>
</Steps>

## Write the portable hook

The hook is an ordinary Rust function generic over `ReactiveContext`. It knows nothing about GPUI, windows, or rendering.

<Code lang="rust" code={`// counter/src/lib.rs
use quoin_core::prelude::*;
use std::rc::Rc;

pub struct Counter<S: Signal<u32>> {
    pub count: S,
    pub increment: Rc<dyn Fn()>,
}

pub fn use_counter<C: ReactiveContext>(cx: &C) -> Counter<C::Signal<u32>> {
    let count = cx.create_signal(0u32);
    let increment = {
        let count = count.clone();
        Rc::new(move || count.update(|c| *c += 1))
    };
    Counter { count, increment }
}`} />

Key points:

- `cx.create_signal(0u32)` allocates reactive state through the context. The returned type is `C::Signal<u32>` — whatever the active framework provides.
- `count.update(|c| *c += 1)` mutates in place and requests a re-render on pull-based adapters.
- The `Signal<T>` trait bound keeps the struct usable with any adapter's signal type.

## Render it in GPUI

Now wire the hook into a GPUI component and bootstrap the app with `run_app!`.

<Code lang="rust" code={`// counter-gpui/src/main.rs
use counter::use_counter;
use quoin::prelude::*;

struct CounterView {
    counter: counter::Counter<quoin::GpuiSignal<u32>>,
    _ctx: GpuiContext,
}

impl Render for CounterView {
    fn render(&mut self, _window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        let count = self.counter.count.get();
        div()
            .flex()
            .child(format!("Count: {count}"))
            .child(
                div()
                    .child("Increment")
                    .on_mouse_down(MouseButton::Left, cx.listener(|this, _, _, _| {
                        (this.counter.increment)();
                    }))
            )
    }
}

fn main() {
    let ctx = GpuiContext::new();
    let counter = use_counter(&ctx);
    run_app!(CounterView { counter, _ctx: ctx });
}`} />

Run it:

<Code lang="sh" code={`cargo run -p counter-gpui`} />

**Expected output:** a native window showing `Count: 0` with an `Increment` button; each click updates the label.

## Re-target the same hook to Leptos

Change the feature flag and swap the view. The hook crate is untouched.

<Code lang="toml" code={`# counter-leptos/Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
counter = { path = "../counter" }
quoin = { version = "0.1", features = ["leptos"] }`} />

<Code lang="rust" code={`// counter-leptos/src/lib.rs
use counter::use_counter;
use quoin::prelude::*;

#[component]
pub fn App() -> impl IntoView {
    let ctx = LeptosContext::new();
    let counter = use_counter(&ctx);
    view! {
        <div>
            <p>"Count: " {move || counter.count.get()}</p>
            <button on:click=move |_| (counter.increment)()>"Increment"</button>
        </div>
    }
}`} />

<Aside type="note">
  Enable exactly one framework feature per crate. Enabling two triggers a `compile_error!` that names the offending configuration — the backends are mutually exclusive by design.
</Aside>

You can also skip the view layer entirely: the [testing guide](/guides/testing/) runs the same hook headlessly with `quoin-testkit`, and the [devtools guide](/guides/devtools/) traces every signal mutation it performs.
